newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga says Vigdis oil development ahead of schedule.
newsitem.headline: Saga says Vigdis oil development ahead of schedule.

text.p: Saga Petroleum ASA said on Monday the Vigdis oilfield in the North Sea could begin production at the end of February, well ahead of schedule.
In May Saga brought forward the start up of Vigdis to April 1 1997 from the original plans of July 1. Later the company announced cost savings of 400 million crowns in the 5.1 billion crown budget.

"The Vigdis project is not only on schedule but also ahead of the timetable in some areas. This opens the prospect that the tie-in to the Snorre platform and other fianl stage work could be completed earlier than expected," the company's weekly newsletter said.
"After previous revisions, oil is currently due to start flowing from the field on April 1. The date could now be brought forward even further, possibly to the end of February."

The field is being developed via seabed installation tied-back to the Snorre platform where oil will be processed. Stabilised crude will be transferred via dedicated pipeline to Gullfaks A for storage and offshore loading into shuttle tankers.
Vigdis output is expected to plateau at 95,000 barrels per day (bpd) over three years. Field life is forecast at 15 years.
Estimated recoverable reserves are put at 24.9 million cubic metres of oil (185 million barrels) of oil and two billion cubic metres of natural gas.
Other partners in the development are Den norske stats oljeselskap AS, Esso, Idemitsu, Norsk Hydro ASA, Elf Petroleum and VEBA AG unit Deminex. -- Oslo newsroom +47 22 42 50 41
